title: Can You Trust Your Preference Models? Stackelberg Games for Alignment
abstract: arXiv:2610.15008v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language models are frequently aligned to human preferences via imperfect evaluators whose errors can be exploited during optimization. We train policies to search for comparisons on which an evaluator may reverse the underlying preference, providing candidates for additional supervision. Since human preferences are unavailable during policy training, we use disagreement among an ensemble of preference models as a proxy for prediction error. We formulate this search as a zero-sum Stackelberg game between two opposing policies, a Leader which tries to minimize disagreement, and a Follower which maximizes it. For a general class of finite contextual Stackelberg games, we establish equilibrium existence and, under regularization, uniqueness and a closed-form characterization. We introduce Stackelberg Mirror Descent-Ascent (SMIDA), a two-timescale algorithm with linear last-iterate convergence in the tabular setting, and develop a neural pol

translated_title: 你能信任你的偏好模型吗？面向对齐的Stackelberg博弈
translated_abstract: 语言模型通常通过不完美的评估器与人类偏好进行对齐，而这些评估器的错误可能在优化过程中被利用。我们训练策略来搜索评估器可能反转底层偏好的比较样本，从而为额外监督提供候选。由于在策略训练期间人类偏好不可用，我们使用偏好模型集成之间的分歧作为预测误差的代理。我们将这一搜索形式化为两个对立策略之间的零和Stackelberg博弈：一个试图最小化分歧的领导者，和一个试图最大化分歧的追随者。对于一类一般性的有限上下文Stackelberg博弈，我们建立了均衡的存在性，并在正则化条件下证明了均衡的唯一性及闭式刻画。我们提出了Stackelberg镜像下降-上升算法（SMIDA），这是一种双时间尺度算法，在表格设置下具有线性最后迭代收敛性，并开发了一个神经策略版本。
tldr: 该论文将搜索评估器可能出错的偏好比较样本问题形式化为零和Stackelberg博弈，并提出了具有线性收敛保证的SMIDA算法，用于在偏好模型对齐中识别需要额外人类监督的样本。
en_tdlr: This paper formulates the search for preference comparisons where evaluators may err as a zero-sum Stackelberg game between opposing leader and follower policies, and introduces SMIDA, a two-timescale algorithm with linear last-iterate convergence, to identify samples requiring additional supervision in preference alignment.
